note:
CC: bug bite R forearm x1 day.
HPI: 34F noticed an itchy red bump after gardening yesterday. No fever, no spreading redness, no lip or throat swelling.
Exam: 1 cm erythematous papule R forearm, no warmth, no streaking.
A/P: Insect bite with local reaction. Cool compresses, avoid scratching. RTC if redness spreads or fever develops.
label_note: One minor problem, cool compresses; return precautions do not count.

note:
22M fell off his bicycle 1 hour ago onto pavement. Small abrasion on the left knee, about 3 x 2 cm, no deep tissue involvement, full ROM, walking normally. Tetanus up to date (booster 2 years ago). Wound cleaned with saline and covered with a nonstick bandage.
Assessment: knee abrasion.
Keep clean and dry, change bandage daily.
label_note: Minor problem, superficial dressing.

note:
45M with 3 days of stuffy nose, mild sore throat and sneezing. Afebrile, no shortness of breath. Exam: clear rhinorrhea, mild pharyngeal erythema without exudate, lungs clear.
Impression: common cold (viral URI), self-limited.
Plan: saline nasal spray OTC, fluids, rest.
label_note: Common cold is self-limited; OTC low risk is the only element at low.

note:
30F here for a work note. Had vomiting and diarrhea 3 days ago, fully resolved since yesterday, eating normally. Vitals normal, abdomen soft and nontender.
Assessment: viral gastroenteritis, resolved. Work note given for 2 missed shifts. No treatment needed.
label_note: Resolved self-limited illness, no treatment.

note:
8 y/o M with mild sunburn on shoulders after a pool day yesterday. He describes the pain himself and answers questions appropriately; mom present. No blisters, no fever, drinking well. Exam: mild erythema across both shoulders, no blistering.
A: first-degree sunburn.
P: aloe gel and children's ibuprofen OTC as needed, sun protection counselling.
label_note: The child gives his own history, so no independent historian.

note:
27M with a wooden splinter in the right index finger since this morning. Visible just under the skin. Removed intact with sterile tweezers, no incision needed. Site cleaned and covered with a bandage.
Assessment: splinter, removed. Watch for signs of infection.
label_note: Minor problem, superficial care.

note:
19F, sore throat x2 days, no cough, no fever at home. T 99.1. Tonsils mildly enlarged without exudate, no cervical adenopathy. Rapid strep ordered: negative.
Assessment: viral pharyngitis.
Plan: salt-water gargles, ibuprofen OTC, return if not improving in 5 days.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated + OTC; one test is not enough for limited data.

note:
40M rolled his right ankle playing basketball last night. Able to bear weight in clinic for 4 steps. Tenderness over the ATFL, no bony tenderness at the malleoli or base of the 5th metatarsal; Ottawa ankle rules negative, so no X-ray.
Assessment: right ankle sprain, grade 1.
Plan: RICE, ankle brace, ibuprofen OTC 400 mg every 6 hours as needed.
label_note: A test considered and not ordered is not counted here.

note:
55F here because she ran out of amlodipine and cannot see her PCP until next month. Hypertension, stable on amlodipine 5 mg; BP today 128/78, no headache, chest pain or swelling.
Assessment: essential hypertension, stable, at goal.
Plan: refilled amlodipine 5 mg daily, 30 days, follow up with PCP.
label_note: One stable chronic illness + a refill: prescription risk alone does not make 99214.

note:
26F with dysuria and urinary frequency for 2 days. No fever, no flank pain, no vaginal discharge. LMP 2 weeks ago. Urinalysis ordered: positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites. Urine culture sent.
Assessment: acute uncomplicated cystitis.
Plan: nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days prescribed, fluids.
label_note: Two unique tests = limited data; only risk reaches moderate.

note:
6 y/o F brought by her mother for right ear pain since last night. History obtained from mother; the patient is too young to give a reliable timeline of her symptoms. Low-grade fever at home, tugging at the ear. Exam: right TM bulging and erythematous, left TM normal.
Assessment: acute otitis media, right.
Plan: amoxicillin 90 mg/kg/day divided twice daily for 10 days prescribed, acetaminophen OTC for pain.
label_note: Independent historian = limited data.

note:
33M with an itchy rash on both forearms after clearing brush 2 days ago, linear vesicles, no facial involvement. Also a small paper cut on the left thumb from yesterday, clean, edges together.
Assessment: 1) contact dermatitis from poison ivy, 2) superficial paper cut.
Plan: hydrocortisone 1% cream OTC twice daily, wash clothing; keep the cut clean.
label_note: Two self-limited problems = low problems; with OTC risk, low; undercoded.

note:
28F with red, irritated left eye and yellow discharge for 2 days, lids stuck together this morning. Vision normal, no photophobia, no contact lens use. Exam: conjunctival injection with purulent discharge, cornea clear.
Assessment: acute bacterial conjunctivitis, left eye.
Plan: erythromycin ophthalmic ointment prescribed, apply 4 times daily for 5 days; hand hygiene.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated + prescription = low.

note:
48M back for a recheck of left lower leg cellulitis, day 5 of cephalexin. Redness has shrunk inside the marked border, no fever, no streaking, walking normally.
Assessment: cellulitis, improving on antibiotics (stable).
Plan: continue cephalexin 500 mg four times daily to complete 7 days, elevate the leg.
label_note: Stable acute illness; continuing a prescription is prescription drug management.

note:
62F with a dry cough for 2 weeks after a cold. No fever, no shortness of breath, nonsmoker. Lungs clear. Chest X-ray ordered; radiology report reviewed: no infiltrate, no effusion. COVID-19 antigen test ordered: negative.
Assessment: post-viral cough.
Plan: honey, dextromethorphan OTC at night, recheck if not better in 2 weeks.
label_note: Two tests = limited; nothing reaches moderate.

note:
35M with low back pain since lifting a heavy box at work yesterday. No numbness, no weakness, no bladder or bowel changes, no fever. Paraspinal muscle tenderness on the right, straight leg raise negative, strength and reflexes normal.
Assessment: acute lumbar strain, no red flags.
Plan: ibuprofen OTC, heat, gentle activity, physical therapy referral if not better in 2 weeks.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated injury + OTC.

note:
11 y/o M, mild intermittent asthma, needs an albuterol inhaler refill for school. Patient reports no wheeze or night cough this month, uses the inhaler before sports only. Lungs clear, SpO2 99%.
Assessment: asthma, well controlled.
Plan: albuterol HFA refilled, school inhaler form completed.
label_note: One stable chronic illness + refill.

note:
24F with nausea and 4 episodes of vomiting since last night, mild diarrhea, roommate had the same. Keeping small sips down. Mild diffuse tenderness, no guarding, mucous membranes slightly dry. Urine pregnancy test ordered: negative.
Assessment: acute viral gastroenteritis without significant dehydration.
Plan: ondansetron 4 mg ODT prescribed, oral rehydration.
label_note: Acute uncomplicated + prescription; one test.

note:
52M with COPD, 3 days of more shortness of breath and more sputum, now yellow. SpO2 94% on room air, expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Chest X-ray ordered; my read: hyperinflation, no infiltrate, no pneumothorax; radiology over-read pending.
Assessment: COPD exacerbation.
Plan: prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 5 days prescribed.
label_note: Own read of the X-ray while the radiologist reads it = independent interpretation (category 2).

note:
29F with burning on urination for 3 days, now fever to 101.9 and right flank pain since this morning. Right CVA tenderness. Urinalysis ordered: positive nitrites and large leukocytes. Urine culture sent. Urine pregnancy test: negative. Tolerating oral fluids, HR 98, BP normal.
Assessment: acute pyelonephritis, no signs of sepsis, appropriate for outpatient treatment.
Plan: cefpodoxime 200 mg twice daily for 10 days prescribed; go to the ED if vomiting or worse.
label_note: Three tests = moderate data; ED is a return precaution, not a decision to hospitalize.

note:
45M seen for medication refills while his PCP is on leave. Hypertension, stable on lisinopril 20 mg, BP 124/80. Type 2 diabetes, stable on metformin 1000 mg twice daily; reviewed his PCP visit note from June: A1c 6.6%. No symptoms.
Assessment: hypertension, stable; type 2 diabetes, at goal.
Plan: lisinopril and metformin refilled for 90 days.
label_note: Two stable chronic illnesses + refills; undercoded.

note:
38F felt a lump in the left breast 1 week ago, not tender, no nipple discharge, no skin change. Exam: 2 cm firm, mobile mass at the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, no axillary nodes.
Assessment: left breast mass, undiagnosed, uncertain prognosis.
Plan: ordered diagnostic mammogram and left breast ultrasound; referred to breast surgery.
label_note: Only problems reach moderate; two tests = limited; non-invasive imaging is low risk.

note:
58F with known asthma, wheezing and chest tightness for 1 day after a cold. SpO2 95%, speaking full sentences, diffuse wheezes. Albuterol-ipratropium nebulizer given in clinic with good improvement, SpO2 97% after.
Assessment: asthma exacerbation, moderate.
Plan: prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days prescribed, continue albuterol as needed.
label_note: Chronic illness with exacerbation + prescription.

note:
41M fell from a ladder onto an outstretched right hand 2 hours ago. Visible deformity of the distal forearm, neurovascularly intact. X-ray of the right wrist ordered; my interpretation: displaced distal radius fracture, radiologist report pending. Discussed with on-call orthopedics, Dr. Patel, who advised splinting and clinic follow-up tomorrow for possible reduction. Sugar-tong splint applied.
Plan: naproxen 500 mg twice daily prescribed, ice, elevation, ortho follow-up tomorrow.
label_note: Interpretation + discussion = extensive data, but only one element is high.

note:
66M with type 2 diabetes, 2 weeks of increased thirst and urination. Fingerstick glucose ordered in clinic: 320. Not vomiting, alert, no abdominal pain. Takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, admits missing doses recently.
Assessment: type 2 diabetes with worsening control (hyperglycemia), no signs of DKA.
Plan: started glipizide 5 mg daily, diet review, PCP follow-up within 1 week.
label_note: Chronic illness with progression + prescription; overcoded at 99215.

note:
3 y/o M with fever to 103 and cough for 3 days. History from father, since the patient is too young to describe his symptoms. Decreased appetite but drinking. RR 32, crackles at the right base, SpO2 95%. Rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests ordered: both negative. Chest X-ray ordered; radiology report reviewed: right lower lobe consolidation.
Assessment: community-acquired pneumonia.
Plan: high-dose amoxicillin prescribed, recheck in 48 hours.
label_note: Three tests + historian = category 1 at moderate.

note:
50M noticed yellow eyes for 4 days, dark urine, no abdominal pain, no fever, minimal alcohol. Scleral icterus, abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly palpable. Reviewed his liver test results from last month at another clinic: normal then. Ordered CMP and CBC today.
Assessment: new painless jaundice, undiagnosed, uncertain prognosis.
Plan: results to be called tomorrow; urgent outpatient GI referral placed; ED if abdominal pain or confusion.
label_note: Outside liver tests + CMP + CBC = 3 category-1 items; undercoded.

note:
33F with a history of migraines, 2 days of her typical headache that has not responded to her usual sumatriptan, more frequent attacks this month. Normal neuro exam, no fever, no neck stiffness.
Assessment: migraine, worsening frequency, not responding to usual treatment.
Plan: ketorolac 30 mg IM given in clinic, rizatriptan prescribed to replace sumatriptan, headache diary, neurology follow-up.
label_note: Chronic illness with exacerbation + prescription; undercoded.

note:
36M hit his head on a cabinet door yesterday and by his own account blacked out for a few seconds, now with a mild headache, no vomiting. GCS 15, normal neuro exam. CT head ordered given the loss of consciousness; radiology report reviewed: no acute intracranial findings.
Assessment: concussion with brief loss of consciousness.
Plan: acetaminophen OTC, cognitive rest, return precautions given.
label_note: Complicated injury but one test and OTC risk: only problems reach moderate.

note:
60M with a red, hot, swollen right big toe since last night, same as his past gout attacks. Known gout, on allopurinol, flare despite treatment. Reviewed his rheumatology clinic note from last year: diagnosis confirmed by joint aspiration then. Afebrile.
Assessment: acute gout flare (chronic gout with exacerbation).
Plan: colchicine prescribed, continue allopurinol, ice and rest.
label_note: Chronic illness with exacerbation + prescription; one external note.

note:
62M with substernal chest pressure for 40 minutes, sweating and nausea. BP 150/92, HR 104, pale and diaphoretic. 12-lead ECG performed in clinic (tracing and interpretation billed separately): ST elevation in the inferior leads. Aspirin 324 mg chewed. Called EMS for emergency transfer to the ED for possible cardiac catheterization and admission. Discussed with the receiving ED physician, Dr. Gomez.
Assessment: acute coronary syndrome, suspected inferior STEMI.
label_note: ECG billed separately is not counted; the discussion is category 3.

note:
25F with periumbilical pain since yesterday that moved to the right lower quadrant, nausea, fever 100.9. RLQ tenderness with rebound and guarding. Urine pregnancy test ordered: negative. Urinalysis ordered: normal.
Assessment: suspected acute appendicitis.
Plan: sent to the emergency department now for surgical evaluation; nothing by mouth.
label_note: Threat to bodily function + decision to escalate care; undercoded.

note:
71F with COPD, worsening shortness of breath for 2 days, now SpO2 86% on room air, RR 28, using accessory muscles. Reviewed her hospital discharge summary from last month for a COPD admission. Chest X-ray ordered. Oxygen started at 2 L by nasal cannula.
Assessment: acute hypoxic respiratory failure, likely COPD exacerbation versus pneumonia.
Plan: transfer to the ED by ambulance for admission.
label_note: Threat to life + decision regarding hospitalization.

note:
45M with severe asthma attack, not improving after 3 albuterol nebulizer treatments in clinic, SpO2 89%, speaking in short phrases, tight air movement.
Assessment: severe asthma exacerbation, not responding to treatment.
Plan: methylprednisolone 125 mg IM given; EMS called for transfer to the ED for admission.
label_note: Chronic illness with severe exacerbation + decision regarding hospitalization.

note:
57M with asthma, wheezing for 2 days after a cold. SpO2 96%, mild expiratory wheezes, speaking full sentences. One albuterol nebulizer in clinic with clear improvement.
Assessment: mild asthma exacerbation.
Plan: prednisone 40 mg for 5 days prescribed, albuterol as needed.
label_note: Exacerbation, not severe; overcoded at 99215.

note:
19M ate a cookie with peanuts 15 minutes ago, now lip swelling, hives, wheezing, BP 85/50. Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM given immediately, EMS called for transfer to the ED.
Assessment: anaphylaxis with hypotension.
Plan: emergency transfer; observed until EMS arrival.
label_note: Threat to life + decision regarding hospitalization.
